title: Catalogue against sales
prompt: Merchandising wants every order line next to its product, and every product that never sold. Write `solve(order_items, products)` so it returns both, with nothing counted twice.
rules: Each row of `order_items` appears exactly as many times as it does in `order_items`, with its product's `name`, or a missing `name` if the product isn't listed.
Each listed product that no line matches appears once, with a missing `order_id` and `line_no`.
The product list sometimes repeats a product row; repeated rows are exact copies. A missing `product_id` never matches anything, in either table.
hints: Rows from both sides must survive, matched or not: that's a `full` join on `product_id`.
A repeated product row would match every line of that product twice. Remove the copies from `products` before the join.
Don't remove duplicates after the join: two identical lines in `order_items` must both stay. A join never matches a missing key, so those rows come through unmatched on their own.
explanation: Remove the product copies first, then keep both sides: `order_items.join(products.dropDuplicates(), on="product_id", how="full").select("product_id", "order_id", "line_no", "name")`. Joining with `on="product_id"` gives one key column filled from whichever side has it, so an unsold product keeps its id. A missing `product_id` never equals anything in a join, so such a line comes out with no name and such a product comes out with no line, each once. A `left` join loses the unsold products, and `distinct()` after the join would merge two genuinely identical lines.
